_README: GPU hardware specifications used for roofline (MBU/MFU) analysis. Units: hbm_bandwidth_gbps is in GB/s (gigabytes per second, 1 GB = 1e9 bytes). peak_flops_tflops gives DENSE (not 2:4 sparse) tensor-core throughput in TFLOPS for each numeric format. Sources: NVIDIA datasheets / whitepapers (H100, A100, L40S, L4, RTX 4090/5090, RTX 6000 Ada, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, A10G, T4). Where a vendor only publishes sparse (2:4) numbers we record half of that as the dense value, consistent with how vLLM/torch report achievable FLOPs. fp8 entries are omitted (null) for GPUs without FP8 tensor cores (Ampere/Turing). These are nominal peak values; achievable throughput is typically 50-80% of peak. Last reviewed 2026-06. peak_flops_tflops.fp4 is the dense FP4 (NVFP4/MXFP4) tensor peak, Blackwell only. Professional/datacenter parts run FP16 tensor math with FP32 accumulate at full rate; GeForce parts at half rate, and the GeForce entries here use the halved (FP32-accumulate) figures that inference kernels actually achieve. Values can be reproduced from SM count x boost clock x per-SM rate with vllm_benchmark.core.hardware.gpu_derive; on an NVIDIA host the suite derives the spec from the device and cross-checks this table (see --gpu-spec).
